# How Do I Manage Inventory of Items Across Properties?


You manage item inventory across properties by giving each property a structured record of its expected items, with restocking tracked and connected to cost. On **Jestor** , this uses the same connected table structure applied to any asset tracking.


Property items, towels, linens, kitchenware, are often tracked informally or not at all, until a guest complaint reveals something is missing.


## What is missing without structured inventory


- No real record of what items each property is supposed to have
- Restocking discovered reactively, when a guest complains
- No cost tracking for restocking by property over time
- Inconsistency between what different properties actually have versus the expected standard


## How structured inventory management works


- Each property has a connected inventory record, listing expected items
- Restocking requests can trigger automatic approval and purchasing
- Restock cost connects back to the specific property
- Periodic audits can be structured as forms, comparing actual versus expected


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Inventory stays connected to the specific property, not a separate spreadsheet
- Automation reduces the reactive discovery of missing items
- Cost tracking supports decisions about standardizing across properties
- The same structure scales from a few properties to a large portfolio


Informal inventory Structured inventory


Discovered by guest complaint Tracked proactively per property


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can this trigger a purchase request automatically?** Yes, when an item needs restocking, depending on automation setup. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can inventory audits be structured as a checklist?** Yes, through forms with conditional logic.


**Is restock cost visible per property?** Yes, connected to the specific property's record.
